condition: Retrosternal multinodular goitre with tracheal compression
summary: 68-year-old woman with a long-standing multinodular goitre, now breathless lying flat, positive Pemberton sign; CT: retrosternal extension 5 cm below the thoracic inlet, trachea narrowed to 8 mm. Compressive goitre: TFTs, CT (done), airway planning, total thyroidectomy (possible sternotomy) — urgent, not routine.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Breathless lying flat and swelling in the neck
inputs.hpi: Goitre for 15 years. Over 4 months: breathless lying flat, wakes choking, noisy breathing when she raises her arms, food sticking occasionally. Voice normal. No palpitations.

exam.general: Large multinodular goitre, lower border not palpable. Pemberton sign positive (facial plethora on raising arms). Trachea deviated to the left. No stridor at rest. SpO2 96%.

imaging.name: CT neck and thorax
imaging.result: Large multinodular goitre with retrosternal extension 5 cm below the thoracic inlet into the anterior mediastinum; trachea deviated and narrowed to 8 mm at the inlet. No lymphadenopathy.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Retrosternal multinodular goitre with tracheal compression (8 mm)
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Compressive retrosternal multinodular goitre — orthopnoea, positive Pemberton sign, trachea narrowed to 8 mm on CT. Euthyroid. Plan total thyroidectomy (cervical approach ± sternotomy, cardiothoracic back-up); anaesthetic airway assessment; vocal cord check.

redFlags.note: Tracheal narrowing with positional dyspnoea is a red flag that must be surfaced.

mustInclude.note: Surgery is the treatment for a compressive retrosternal goitre.

guideline.name: NICE NG145 — Thyroid disease: assessment and management
guideline.section: Non-malignant thyroid enlargement: investigation and referral (compressive symptoms, stridor); surgery for compressive goitre
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Thyroid disease: assessment and management. NICE guideline NG145. London: NICE; 2019.

rationale: Base compressive-goitre case: urgent surgical but not an emergency today (no stridor at rest). Tests that tracheal compression is flagged and surgery is planned.
